stem: Which of these is NOT an acceptable way to handle ready-to-eat food, such as a deli sandwich?
choices: Washing your hands well, then touching the food with bare hands
oneLineConcept: No bare hands on ready-to-eat food
explanation:
**Ready-to-eat food** (food that will not be cooked again) must **not be touched with bare hands**, even right after washing. Use **single-use gloves, tongs, spatulas, or deli tissue**.

**Wrong choices**
- Using single-use gloves: Single-use gloves are an acceptable way to handle ready-to-eat food.
- Using tongs: Tongs are an acceptable way to handle ready-to-eat food.
- Using deli tissue (wax paper): Deli tissue is an acceptable way to handle ready-to-eat food.
reviewNote: Separate re-solve matched the answer, but flagged it: some state/local codes allow limited bare-hand contact with ready-to-eat food under an approved alternative procedure (FDA Food Code 2022 3-301.11(D)), so "NOT acceptable" depends on local rules. Not published until reworded and re-verified.
